record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays unboundedly far from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must the integer-part family {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} then be good for ℓ-recurrence for a single transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Let F be as above and suppose that for every function a ∈ span∗(F) we have |a(t) − cp(t)| → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]. Show that the collection of sequences {([a1(n)]), . . . ,([a`(n)])} is good for `-recurrence of a single transformation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Hardy field is a field of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on some half-line $[t_0,\infty)$ that is closed under differentiation. A function $a$ in such a field has polynomial growth if there exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $a(t)/t^d\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. 

Let $F=\{a_1,\dots,a_\ell\}$ be functions from some Hardy field, all of polynomial growth, and let $\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ denote the set of nontrivial real linear combinations $c_1 a_1+\cdots+c_\ell a_\ell$ with $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell)\in\mathbb{R}^\ell\setminus\{0\}$. Assume that for every $a\in\operatorname{span}^*(F)$, every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and every $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$,
$$|a(t)-c\,p(t)|\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }t\to\infty.$$

A family of integer-valued sequences $(b_1(n)),\dots,(b_\ell(n))$ is called good for $\ell$-recurrence (for a single transformation) if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-b_1(n)}A\cap T^{-b_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-b_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

Prove that under the hypothesis above, the family $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence for a single transformation.
artifact.category_tag: Multiple ergodic averages along Hardy field sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress on this type of conjecture has appeared in recent work on multiple ergodic averages along Hardy-field functions (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Moreira–Richter–Robertson, "Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field," 2020/2024), which confirms several of Frantzikinakis's conjectures and yields recurrence/combinatorial consequences for such families, including mixtures of polynomial and non-polynomial Hardy functions. However, available sources do not state that the precise problem (in full generality, only under the unbounded-distance-from-real-multiples-of-integer-polynomials hypothesis) is fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field: convergence, recurrence and combinatorial applications
status_evidence.snippet: We obtain new results pertaining to convergence and recurrence of multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field... confirms some of the conjectures posed by Frantzikinakis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work resolves several of Frantzikinakis's Hardy-field recurrence conjectures, giving partial progress relevant to this problem.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on multiple ergodic averages, including Problem 25 on Hardy-field recurrence.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was posed as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's problem list.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity - 40 years on
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of progress on joint ergodicity criteria for Hardy sequences and related families.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys discuss progress but do not record this problem as fully solved.
